title: Regularization
subtitle: L1, L2, dropout, and preventing overfitting

content.text: Overfitting means the model memorises training data. Regularization adds a penalty on large coefficients to keep the model simple.

content.code:
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge, Lasso, ElasticNet

# Ridge (L2): penalises sum of squared coefficients
ridge = Ridge(alpha=1.0)  # alpha controls penalty strength
ridge.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Lasso (L1): drives some coefficients to exactly 0 (feature selection)
lasso = Lasso(alpha=0.1)
lasso.fit(X_train, y_train)
print("Non-zero features:", sum(lasso.coef_ != 0))

content.definition: Penalises the sum of squared weights. Keeps all features but shrinks them.
Penalises the sum of absolute weights. Drives unimportant features to zero.

questions.question: Which regularization method performs feature selection?
questions.explanation: L1 (Lasso) regularization sets the coefficients of unimportant features to zero, effectively removing them.

faq.q: How do I choose the regularization strength (alpha)?
faq.a: Use cross-validation and GridSearchCV to search over a range of alpha values and pick the one with best validation score.
